villages.name: Matsudaira
villages.note: Hill-valley village where the Matsudaira (later Tokugawa) clan began; clan temple Kōgetsu-in.

villages.name: Asuke
villages.note: Chūma road post village where coastal salt was repacked for the mountains ('Asuke salt').

villages.name: Busetsu
villages.note: Inabu uplands post village below the ruined Busetsu castle.

villages.name: Hiraya
villages.note: High pass village on the Mikawa-Shinano border; forestry and charcoal. Namiai checkpoint is 8 km on.

villages.name: Komaba
villages.note: Achi post village; the story says Takeda Shingen died near here in 1573.

villages.name: Iijima
villages.note: Ina valley village with the shogunate's intendant office (Iijima jin'ya, 1677).

villages.name: Miyada
villages.note: Ina road post village on the Tenryū terraces below the Central Alps.

villages.name: Matsushima
villages.note: Minowa's Ina road post village at the north end of the Ina valley.

villages.name: Mori
villages.note: Market village at the foot of the Akiba road; Oguni shrine (Tōtōmi's first shrine) nearby.

villages.name: Inui
villages.note: Gate village for Akiha-san, below the ruined Inui castle; pilgrims' inns.

villages.name: Misakubo
villages.note: Mountain market village below Aokuzure pass; Nishiure dengaku field-dance.

villages.name: Wada
villages.note: Chief village of the Tōyama valley; Shimotsuki fire-and-hot-water festival.

villages.name: Kashio
villages.note: Ōshika village with a mountain salt spring ('deer salt'), rare far from the sea.

villages.name: Ichinose
villages.note: Hase valley relay village below Bunkui pass, on the way to Takatō.

villages.name: Manzawa
villages.note: Border relay village between Suruga and Kai on the Fuji River road.

villages.name: Nanbu
villages.note: Relay village on the Fuji River; the place the Nanbu clan took its name from.

villages.name: Kajikazawa
villages.note: Head port of the Fuji River boats (from 1607): Kai's tax rice went down, Suruga salt came up.

villages.name: Kurokoma
villages.note: Misaka road village; named for the legendary black horse of Kai.

villages.name: Subashiri
villages.note: Fuji pilgrims' east trailhead; buried under the 1707 Hōei eruption ash and rebuilt.

villages.name: Mizonokuchi
villages.note: Ōyama road post village at the Futako ferry over the Tama River.

villages.name: Atsugi
villages.note: Sagami River ferry and market village on the Ōyama road.

villages.name: Ōyama
villages.note: Pilgrim-lodge (oshi) village at the foot of Ōyama and its Afuri shrine; Edo craftsmen came in summer.

villages.name: Sekimoto
villages.note: Post village at the foot of Ashigara pass; gate of the Daiyūzan Saijō-ji temple.

villages.name: Fukara
villages.note: Watered by the Hakone irrigation tunnel from Lake Ashi (finished 1670).

villages.name: Seya
villages.note: Relay village of the Nakahara road on the Sagami upland.

villages.name: Sakashita
villages.note: Shimo-kaidō stage below Utsu pass.

villages.name: Tajimi
villages.note: Shimo-kaidō village on the Toki River; Mino-ware kilns in the hills around.

villages.name: Komaki
villages.note: Post village (laid out 1623-28) under Komaki-yama, Nobunaga's castle hill and Ieyasu's 1584 camp.

villages.name: Tsuge
villages.note: Iga border post village below Kabuto pass; ninja country, and one of Bashō's claimed birthplaces.

villages.name: Kasagi
villages.note: Village under Kasagi-dera, Emperor Go-Daigo's 1331 mountain stronghold, on the Kizu River.

villages.name: Kizu
villages.note: River port on the Kizu where timber and goods for Nara were landed.

villages.name: Hiraoka
villages.note: Village at Hiraoka shrine (Kawachi's first shrine), foot of the Kuragari pass.

villages.name: Hino
villages.note: Home village of the Hino merchants (Ōmi pedlars); lacquerware and travelling medicine.

villages.name: Nagasawa
villages.note: Saku road relay village on the Yatsugatake skirts.

villages.name: Umi-no-kuchi
villages.note: Upland relay village; Umi-no-kuchi castle, where young Takeda Shingen won his first fight (1536, legend).

villages.name: Takanomachi
villages.note: Relay and market village in the upper Chikuma valley.

villages.name: Oyashiki
villages.note: Village around Erin-ji, the Takeda family temple with Shingen's grave; Katsunuma's vineyards are 7 km south.

villages.name: Ashikura
villages.note: Last village below the Southern Alps (today's Ashiyasu); forestry and charcoal.

villages.name: Yamura
villages.note: Gunnai market village on the Katsura River; Gunnai silk (kaiki). Castle town until 1704.

villages.name: Dōshi
villages.note: Long valley village on the Dōshi road between Sagami and Lake Yamanaka; charcoal.

villages.name: Umegashima
villages.note: Head of the Abe valley; old gold diggings and a hot spring.

villages.name: Utōgi
villages.note: Abe valley hamlet said to be where wasabi was first grown (early 1600s), presented to Ieyasu.

villages.name: Ieyama
villages.note: Ōi River valley village (Kawane); tea and timber rafts.

villages.name: Futamata
villages.note: Tenryū River landing for timber rafts; Futamata castle ruin (Nobuyasu's death, 1579). On the Hamamatsu branch of the Akiba road.

villages.name: Kiga
villages.note: Himekaidō checkpoint village at the north inlet of Lake Hamana (checkpoint from 1601).

villages.name: Nagashino
villages.note: Village under Nagashino castle; the 1575 battlefield of Shitaragahara is just west.

villages.name: Taguchi
villages.note: Chief village of the Shitara uplands on the Mikawa-Shinano back road.

villages.name: Nagakute
villages.note: Farming village on the 1584 Komaki-Nagakute battlefield.

villages.name: Seki
villages.note: Mino sword-smiths' village (Seki blades); also knives and tools.

villages.name: Warabi
villages.note: Makidani paper village: hon-Minogami, the best shōji paper.

villages.name: Takasu
villages.note: Ring-levee (wajū) village in the Kiso-Nagara-Ibi delta; Takasu domain seat from 1700.

villages.name: Tsushima
villages.note: Village-town around Tsushima shrine; summer lantern-boat festival; river port.

villages.name: Shigaraki
villages.note: Shigaraki pottery kilns; its tea jars carried the shogun's Uji tea.

villages.name: Kashiwara
villages.note: Kawachi cotton village at the new Yamato River mouth (rerouted 1704); Kashiwara cargo boats.

villages.name: Tokorozawa
villages.note: Market village on the dry Musashino upland.

villages.name: Ōme
villages.note: Tama River rafting village at the edge of the hills; Ōme-jima striped cloth.

villages.name: Ōhara
villages.note: Hill village north-east of Kyoto on the Wakasa (mackerel) road; Ōhara women carried firewood to the city; Sanzen-in.

villages.name: Chichibu
villages.note: Chichibu Ōmiya: Chichibu shrine, silk markets and the 34 Kannon pilgrimage.

villages.name: Nojima
villages.note: Kanazawa fishing village by the Eight Views of Kanazawa; salt pans nearby.

villages.name: Misaki
villages.note: Tip of Miura: tuna and bonito boats, and an anchorage for ships bound for Edo.

villages.name: Manazuru
villages.note: Fishing and stone-quarry village; its Komatsu stone built Edo castle's walls.

villages.name: Itō
villages.note: Izu fishing village where William Adams built Western ships for Ieyasu (1604-05).

villages.name: Heda
villages.note: Fishing village in a sheltered hook-shaped harbour on west Izu.

villages.name: Omaezaki
villages.note: Cape fishing village with the shogunate's beacon (Miobi light, 1635).

villages.name: Irago
villages.note: Fishing village at the tip of Atsumi; Bashō visited in 1687.

villages.name: Morozaki
villages.note: Fishing village at the tip of Chita.

villages.name: Tokoname
villages.note: Chita coast kiln-and-harbour village: Tokoname jars shipped by sea.

villages.name: Shiroko
villages.note: Ise-bay port and fishing village; Ise katagami dye-stencil makers.

villages.name: Kitakomatsu
villages.note: Lake Biwa fishing village under the Hira mountains.

villages.name: Sugaura
villages.note: Self-governing lakeside fishing village with gated entrances, north Lake Biwa.
